title: The Thread Map
motto: The website is the map. The Trap House is the live room. The Trap Pass gets you deeper inside.

scenes.name: Author Profile Map
scenes.alt: Author profile map with figure stations, shelves, flags, cats, a notebook reading Paradise or Oblivion, and project objects.
scenes.description: The profile map collects different shareable parts of Ryan's story, surrounded by the archive, the cats, the shelves, the pressure, and the floor-note fork between paradise and oblivion.

hotspots.label: Shock Title Figure
hotspots.story: The left-edge figure carries the title shock. Its job is to open attention, then immediately route people into context: book, documentary, archive, and witness material.

hotspots.label: Archive Spark
hotspots.story: This station turns spectacle into record: the strange outfit, the cats, the visual joke, and the energy of building a project out of scattered footage.

hotspots.label: Platform War Figure
hotspots.story: The masked jersey figure represents bans, rebuilds, audience migration, and the move from disposable feeds into a website, Discord, email list, and owned archive.

hotspots.label: Labor / Survival Figure
hotspots.story: This station holds work, exhaustion, survival math, and the practical life underneath the bigger mythology. The archive stays grounded because real pressure keeps showing up.

hotspots.label: Hockey Body Figure
hotspots.story: The goalie-body station is about impact, performance, armor, injury, and control. It is the body trying to hold the line while the rest of the map keeps moving.

hotspots.label: Exposure Loop
hotspots.story: This uncomfortable station is about self-documenting in public: embarrassment, collapse, humor, shame, performance, and the risk of becoming evidence before you understand yourself.

hotspots.label: System Mirror Jersey
hotspots.story: The jersey figure points to Crack Capitalism as a system mirror: private compulsion, public reward loops, platform pressure, and a culture built around never enough.

hotspots.label: Deep File Figure
hotspots.story: The black-mask station is the deeper-house route: locked drops, Trap House work, archive witnesses, and the parts that only make sense after someone understands the map.

hotspots.label: Cats / Home Signal
hotspots.story: The cats are not decoration. They are the home signal, the tenderness thread, and the proof that softness survived inside hard material.

hotspots.label: Spoken-Word TV
hotspots.story: The background screen is reserved for the spoken-word intro. Once Ryan drops the clip, it becomes the voice before visitors start picking up the figures.

hotspots.label: Crack Athlete Crates
hotspots.story: The crates are the collectible layer: passes, waves, roles, badges, drops, and member status as proof that someone was here while the house opened.

hotspots.label: Paradise Or Oblivion Notebook
hotspots.story: The floor notebook is the thesis in object form: every thread asks whether the same evidence becomes collapse or construction, oblivion or something built to last.

scenes.name: Profile Control Room
scenes.alt: Wider author profile room with record crates, support button, and project UI panels.
scenes.description: The wider room shot shows the author stations inside the larger interface: music, support, drops, links, the profile lineup, and the next doors.

hotspots.label: Harm Reduction Info
hotspots.story: This stays practical and human: resources, hotline-style links, and low-judgment support. The room can be raw without being careless.

hotspots.label: Crack Athlete Crates
hotspots.story: The crates turn merch, books, collector cards, and limited drops into one physical station. This is the pass-holder drop mechanic as the house opens.

hotspots.label: Profile Lineup
hotspots.story: Each figure is a version, role, mask, or chapter of the same author. The lineup works like character-select navigation without inventing unrelated characters.

hotspots.label: Join The YouTube
hotspots.story: The public video pipe: trailers, shorts, archive clips, channel updates, and the main funnel back to the room.

scenes.name: Collector Bookshelf
scenes.alt: Bookshelf with author-profile figure packages, Dopesick books, and project collectibles.
scenes.description: The bookshelf is the physical archive: author-profile packages, books, evidence labels, collector objects, and proof the project has a history.

hotspots.label: Roon N' Poon
hotspots.story: The boxed figure shelf gives the profile room a collector's logic: story cards, shelf objects, and unlockable proof from the same archive.

hotspots.label: Dopesick Shelf
hotspots.story: The books anchor the whole project in authorship instead of spectacle. The shelf can become a chapter map, excerpt vault, and proof wall.

hotspots.label: IHOCAIHAG Book
hotspots.story: The main book object routes to excerpts, chapter status, preorder drops, and pass-holder reading rooms.

hotspots.label: Evidence Label
hotspots.story: The evidence label is the archive taxonomy: date, clip, transcript, frame, and story context.

scenes.name: Author Frame
scenes.alt: Ryan holding a framed childhood photo in the room.
scenes.description: The author image with the framed childhood photo brings the room back to the human center: memory, origin, family, and why the archive matters.

hotspots.label: Origin Frame
hotspots.story: The framed photo becomes an origin object: childhood, memory, inheritance, damage, humor, and why the story keeps looping back.

hotspots.label: Pink Hoodie Figure
hotspots.story: This connects the hoodie figure in the lineup to the real person. It makes the toy aesthetic feel personal instead of generic.
